requirement: The annual peak series covers every water year in the period of record with no gaps
Each peak is the highest discharge in its water year, taken from the maximum of the continuous record
evidence: requires the continuous gauge record; this package holds one annual value per water year and cannot confirm the within-year maximum

requirement: The station rating curve is current, and shifts in it are documented
evidence: quality control reports rating-curve fit PASS and rating-curve outlier years WARN; a fit check cannot establish the rating *history*, which must come from the gauge records

requirement: The datum used is the same throughout, and is stated
evidence: peak water levels in this study are referenced to the zero gauge; the reduction datum must be stated on the drawing

requirement: Dredging, diversion, construction or reservoir changes in the channel are assessed for non-stationarity
evidence: not assessable from the discharge series; the last two decades of this record show a clear regime change that must be explained

requirement: Outlying values have been screened and the screening is recorded
evidence: three screens run, nothing deleted: Rosenblatt flags a candidate but the others do not, which is the usual outcome; a single test on 57 points is weak evidence

requirement: A test of the null hypothesis of stationarity is applied
evidence: Mann-Kendall tau = -0.600 (p = 0.548); Pettitt change point at index 50 (p = 0.211).  A detected change point is a physical question for a hydrologist, not a statistical verdict

requirement: The record length is adequate for the return periods being reported, or the limitation is stated
evidence: n = 57 years; return periods at or beyond the record length are flagged in the design table and every period carries a Monte Carlo interval

requirement: Where the record is too short for the required return period, independent evidence is used
evidence: peaks-over-threshold was attempted and refused: only 28 exceedances over 57 years (minimum required 30); the shape estimate is not defensible; the shape interval [-0.556, -0.333] lies entirely below zero, i.e. the data cannot exclude a bounded upper tail; this contradicts the Gumbel and LP3 block-maxima curves

requirement: The log-Pearson III is fitted to the logarithms of the annual maxima
evidence: LP3 on ln Q by Bulletin 17B moments, Cs = 0.096, n = 57

requirement: The skew coefficient lies inside the Bulletin 17B table bounds for the record length
evidence: Cs = 0.096 +/- 0.324 (se), one-sided tail probability 0.192 against the critical value 0.90; within the sampling distribution; the fitted skewness is used directly

requirement: The zero flood is accounted for, and the log transform is legitimate
evidence: no zero or negative discharges appear in this record; a record containing zeros cannot be fitted on a logarithmic scale

requirement: Confidence limits are computed and reported with the design flood
evidence: log-space parametric bootstrap on the Bulletin 17B estimators, 2,000 replicates at 95%

requirement: Independent methods are used as a check on the adopted distribution
evidence: candidates fitted and compared on AICc with goodness-of-fit gates: LN2, LP3, Gumbel

requirement: The observed points are plotted on the frequency curve and the fit is judged visually as well as statistically
evidence: the record-on-curve figure plots all 57 observed maxima against the adopted curve

requirement: An arithmetic check is performed on the adopted curve
evidence: the Bulletin 17B quantile function is evaluated against an independent numerically inverted CDF in the test suite

requirement: The frequency curve is extrapolated only to the periods the data can support
evidence: every period at or beyond the record length is flagged in the design table and carries the Monte Carlo interval

requirement: Bulletin 17B/B17C recommends that for n below about 25 years the confidence limits are treated as approximate
